goal.summary: Enforce a skill-first dispatch routing policy in csm-orchestrate runtime: the orchestrator must check the csm skill library first for every phase task and route substantial work (planning, building, reviewing, scanning, researching, testing) to the matching csm skill executor. Small incidental tasks (running a test suite, checking syntax, formatting, file existence checks, payload repacking) may use the orchestrator own tools and command calls directly. Skills are the default for substantive work; own tools are the default for incidental checks. The routing decision and its enforcement live entirely in the csm-orchestrate runtime (preflight + adapter selection) — NOT in csm-plan. csm-plan remains a simple task list with no dispatch routing schema changes. Additionally, the bootstrap verification output gains trust markers (F-006/F-007), the G7 runner path handling is fixed (F-023), host root derivation uses fileURLToPath (F-024), adapter-required-tests spawns get timeouts (F-025), SHELL_DENYLIST is documented as advisory (F-026), and README documents the orchestrator driver (F-017/F-018).

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: The dispatch policy is skill-first routing, not a blanket prohibition: the orchestrator checks the skill library first for every phase task. Substantial work (planning, building, reviewing, scanning, researching) routes to the matching csm skill executor. Small incidental tasks (test runs, syntax checks, formatting, file operations) use the orchestrator own tools directly. Any use of own tools for skill-level work requires explicit user approval.
assumptionsAndDecisions.evidence: user directive: "its ok for csm orchestrate to determine to use its own tools and command calls for small checks and tasks but not if the task is better off performed by an available skill. it should check the skill library first, and route a task to either its own tools for small incidental tasks or to the skill. skills should be used by default but small tasks can be done outside if a skill."

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: The createHostInvocationAdapter is retained for incidental tasks and testing — it is the sanctioned path for small checks (test runs, syntax checks, formatting) that do not require a full skill lifecycle. It MUST NOT be used for skill-level work (planning, building, reviewing) when a matching skill executor exists. The dispatch policy routes substantial work to the executor adapter.
assumptionsAndDecisions.evidence: the adapter is needed for the 330-test battery; deleting it would break every existing test

assumptionsAndDecisions.statement: The agent-session dispatch protocol (spawning an agent to run csm-plan/csm-build SKILL.md) is a follow-up implementation task — this plan registers the adapters and enforcement but the actual agent-session spawning protocol is the first implementation task

dispatchPolicy.rule: Check the skill library first. Route substantial work to the matching csm skill executor. Use own tools for small incidental tasks.
dispatchPolicy.skillLevelWork: planning, building, reviewing, scanning, researching, test-generation, BDD-mutation, DDD-analysis — MUST route to the matching csm skill executor when one exists
dispatchPolicy.incidentalTasks: running test suites, checking syntax, formatting, file existence, payload repacking, reading files — MAY use the orchestrator own tools and shell commands directly
dispatchPolicy.default: skills are the default for substantive work; own tools are the default for incidental checks
dispatchPolicy.enforcementLocation: csm-orchestrate runtime: preflight (route classification) + adapter selection (executor vs host invocation)
dispatchPolicy.escalation: if the orchestrator determines that a task initially classified as incidental requires skill-level work, it must escalate to the matching skill executor

design.handlers: Each of the 8 csm-build-owned skills gets a csmBuildHandoff adapter whose execute() callback invokes the skill implementation. For instruction-led skills, execute() will eventually spawn an agent session; initially returns blocked/agent-session-required. The existing direct handlers for csm-ddd/csm-scan/csm-upload are already correct.
design.routing: The preflight in skill-executor-preflight.mjs classifies each routeNode: skill-level (route matches a SUPPORTED_SKILLS entry with a registered executor handler) or incidental (no matching handler, route is a small-check task). Skill-level routes without handlers are BLOCKED. Incidental tasks pass through without a handler requirement. The classification happens at dispatch time in the orchestrate runtime, not at plan-authoring time.
design.driver: The driver retains both paths: executorAdapter for skill-level work and hostInvocationAdapter for incidental work. The dispatch policy routes between them per task.
design.bootstrap: The bin verification output gains trustLevel and keyringEnvironment fields so the machine contract is unambiguous about what verify results mean.
